what_it_is: A phone photo (576x1024 portrait) of a ViewSonic monitor, deliberately framed on the LEFT SIDEBAR of a draft personal academic site being previewed inside a claude.ai artifact preview panel. The browser is a Chromium/Chrome window in dark theme with one tab, "Build webpage with provided files", and the artifact toolbar shows the preview named "Korkut's Research Hub". The visible page is a two-column layout: a fixed-width warm cream/parchment sidebar on the left carrying a circular profile photo, a serif name block, a two-line sans subtitle and a vertical nav list of eight visible items with "Home" in the active state; to the right, a cooler near-white content column whose serif navy H1 ends in "PhD" followed by sans body copy with hairline horizontal rules. Nothing is being interacted with — the mouse cursor is parked in the content column, not over any nav item, so no hover state is captured. The preview viewport is shorter than the page: a classic scrollbar with up/down arrows sits at the sidebar/content boundary, its thumb roughly three-quarters of the track and offset downward, which means the top of the profile photo is clipped by the viewport and the nav list continues below the visible "Blog".
app_or_tool: Chromium-based browser (Chrome, dark theme) on Windows, displayed on a ViewSonic monitor (brand wordmark on the bezel, bottom of frame). Evidence: rounded dark tab shape with a close "x" and a "+" new-tab button at the tab strip right; a Claude/Anthropic gradient-swirl favicon; tab title "Build webpage with provided files"; a dark omnibox showing a UUID-style URL with an `?artifact=project%3A...` query. Inside the page: the claude.ai artifact preview panel chrome — a list/outline icon, a circular collapse button with inward diagonal arrows, an active blue-outlined pill reading (globe icon) "Korkut's Research Hub", then a document icon, a "</>" code icon and a layers/stack icon in one dark rounded group, and at the far right a monitor/desktop viewport-toggle icon and a circular user avatar (partially cropped). The preview iframe has rounded top-left and bottom-left corners against the dark panel.

palette: Sidebar background — warm cream / parchment / ivory. Raw camera value ≈ #E4D3B2 at mid-height; white-balance corrected estimate ≈ #F5EFE0 to #F7F2E4. Measured against the content column in the SAME horizontal band at 17 different heights, the sidebar is consistently 24-27% higher in R, 21-24% higher in G but only 8-12% higher in B — a stable ratio down the whole column. That is a real, uniform yellow/ivory cast, not glare. This is THE signature colour of the design.

Content-area background — cooler, near-neutral off-white. Raw ≈ #B2AAA0 (the right side of the frame is underexposed because the phone metered on the sidebar); corrected estimate ≈ #FAFAF8 / #F7F7F5. The essential point for a rebuild: sidebar = warm cream, content = neutral near-white. They are NOT the same colour, and the contrast between them is what separates the two columns — there is no visible border or divider line between them.

Active nav row fill — the same hue as the sidebar, ≈6% darker in luminance (raw 213 → 200 mean). Corrected estimate ≈ #EDE5D0 on a #F5EFE0 ground, equivalent to roughly rgba(0,0,0,0.05) or a warm tint overlay. Subtle, not a strong highlight.

Active-item accent bar — brick / terracotta red. Most-saturated raw pixel (159, 96, 87), R−G = 63; normalised against the adjacent cream ≈ #B5564A to #C0604F. Warm, muted, earthy — NOT a bright primary red. Almost certainly sampled from the red brick wall in the profile photo.
Name text ("Korkut Kaynardag, PhD") — very dark ink with a cool/navy cast, raw darkest #151D12; corrected ≈ #1A2432 / #16202B. Reads as near-black-navy rather than pure black.
Content H1 ("…PhD") — a distinctly BLUE navy, clearly bluer than the sidebar name. Raw darkest #122536; corrected ≈ #1B3A5C / #17365D. This is the accent colour of the content column.
Inactive nav label — warm dark grey / grey-brown. Raw darkest #5E5943; corrected ≈ #52504A / #57534A. Noticeably lighter than the name.

Active nav label ("Home") — measurably darker than its neighbours: darkest ink 60 / 5th-percentile 86, versus About Me at 88 / 106 and Gallery at 92 / 116 in the same exposure band. Corrected ≈ #2C2E2A or near the name colour. The active item darkens its label, and may also step up a weight.
Sub-label ("System Identification · Estimation · Optimization") — lighter grey than the nav labels. Raw darkest #787167; corrected ≈ #857F74 / #8A8478.

Subtitle block ("Assistant Professor…" / "Izmir Institute of Technology") — mid grey, raw darkest #595839; corrected ≈ #55534B. Same tone family as the inactive nav labels, slightly lighter than the name.

Browser chrome (not the site): dark slate #1E2733-ish tab strip and omnibox; the artifact toolbar is near-black #23262B with an active blue pill — text and 1px border ≈ #5B9DF7 / #6AA8FF over a faint translucent blue fill.

CAUTION on every hex above: phone-camera-on-monitor capture, so everything is warm-shifted and the frame carries an exposure falloff to the right and bottom. The white-balance corrections were computed from the brightest 1% of the page region. Use the RELATIONSHIPS (sidebar warmer and lighter than content; active row ~6% darker than sidebar; accent = brick red from the portrait) rather than the literal hex values.
design.typography:
TWO families, cleanly split by role.

SERIF — used for the sidebar name "Korkut Kaynardag, PhD" and for the content-column H1 ending "…PhD". A transitional/old-style serif with marked thick-thin modulation, bracketed serifs, a high-contrast bowl on the D and a distinct ball-less terminal. Reads like Source Serif 4, Lora, Crimson Pro, Libre Baskerville or a Georgia-class face. Weight sits at medium/semibold (600-ish) for the name — it is noticeably heavier than regular but is not a black. No letter-spacing adjustment visible; tracking is normal to very slightly tight. Cap-height plus descender measures 24 photo px, implying a font-size ≈1.7× the nav label (≈26-28px if the nav is 16px). Detail worth reproducing: within the name, "PhD" renders marginally shorter in cap-height than the leading "K" — possibly a smaller or small-caps span, possibly only an optical effect of the render; treat as low-confidence.

SANS — used for everything else: the two-line subtitle, every nav label, and the sub-label, plus the entire content body copy. A neutral geometric-humanist grotesque: double-storey 'a', single-storey 'g', straight-tailed 'y', flat-topped 't', short-armed 'r', a 'G' with a straight spur, a plain 'I' with no crossbars. Strongly consistent with Inter; Helvetica Now, Aktiv Grotesk or a system-UI stack would also fit. All sans text is REGULAR weight (400) — nothing in the sidebar is bold except the active item's slight darkening, and in the content column only the inline run "mysel[f]" is bold.

Relative sizing (all ratios against the nav label = 1.0):
- name, serif                     ≈ 1.7×
- nav label, sans                 = 1.0×
- subtitle, sans                  ≈ 0.75×
- sub-label, sans                 ≈ 0.62×
Line-height: the subtitle wraps on a ≈1.6 line-height. Nav rows sit on a ≈3.0× font-size pitch, but that is padding, not leading — see layout.

No uppercase, no small-caps, no letter-spaced labels, no all-caps section headers anywhere in the sidebar. Every nav label is sentence case as written.
design.layout:
Two-column shell. LEFT: a fixed-width sidebar, 383 photo-px wide (≈300-320 CSS px on the most plausible scale), running the full height of the viewport. RIGHT: a fluid content column that begins immediately after it and extends past the right edge of the photo, so its max-width and right margin are NOT recoverable.

Sidebar internal rhythm, top to bottom: [top padding — clipped, unknown] → circular photo (140px diameter, ≈36.6% of the sidebar width) → 29px gap → serif name → 15px gap → three-line grey subtitle → 36px gap → the nav list.

One left gutter governs everything: ≈18-20 photo px (≈5% of the sidebar width) from the sidebar's left edge. The photo, the name, the subtitle, every nav label and the sub-label all start on it. The nav list is FLAT — no indentation at any level, including under "Signal Processing & Optimization".

Nav vertical rhythm: a constant 47-px pitch per item, of which the interactive band is 43 px and the gap between bands is ≈4 px. Within a band the label's cap sits 15 px below the band top and the baseline 17 px above the band bottom — i.e. roughly symmetrical ≈10px vertical padding around a ~23px line box. The one row carrying a sub-label grows by ≈21 px (68px pitch instead of 47) rather than compressing.

Content column: generous top whitespace above the H1, with THIN FULL-WIDTH HORIZONTAL HAIRLINE RULES used as section separators — one at y≈266 (above the H1) and another at y≈710 (below the second paragraph). Body paragraphs are separated by a clear blank-line gap.

No visible divider, border or shadow between the sidebar and the content column — the two are separated purely by the warm-cream vs neutral-white background contrast.

Vertical rhythm summary in photo px: 15 (name→subtitle) · 22-26 (subtitle line pitch) · 36 (subtitle block→first nav band) · 47 (nav pitch) · 4 (nav gap) · 21 (sub-label increment).
design.navigation:
Order is unambiguous and complete for what is visible, top to bottom:
1. Home                                    ← ACTIVE
2. About Me
3. My Research Areas
4. Gallery
5. Vibrations and Waves
6. Signal Processing & Optimization
     System Identification · Estimation · Optimization    ← sub-label, second line, same left edge
7. Machine Learning
8. Blog                                    ← last visible, clipped by the viewport bottom

Structure: one flat list. Items 5, 6 and 7 are conceptually the three research areas but are rendered at the SAME indent level as Home / About Me / Gallery / Blog, with no group heading, no divider, no indent and no icons. There is no visual grouping mechanism in the sidebar at all — no section rules, no eyebrow labels, no accordions, no chevrons, no expand/collapse affordance.

Sub-labels are used on exactly ONE item. "Signal Processing & Optimization" carries "System Identification · Estimation · Optimization" beneath it at ≈0.62× size in a lighter grey; "Vibrations and Waves" and "Machine Learning" carry none. I checked the pixel rows beneath both of those at a lowered ink threshold to rule out a washed-out sub-label — there is genuinely nothing there. This asymmetry is the single most likely unfinished detail in the design.

ACTIVE-ITEM INDICATOR — three simultaneous cues, all present on "Home":
  (a) A full-bleed horizontal band, 43 px tall, spanning the ENTIRE sidebar width edge to edge (measured continuous from x 51 out to x 428, sidebar ends at 434). SQUARE corners — it is not a rounded pill and it is not inset from the gutter. Fill is the sidebar hue ≈6% darker.
  (b) A vertical ACCENT BAR flush against the sidebar's left edge, x 50-53 (≈3-4 photo px, so ≈3px CSS), y 485-527 — exactly the same height as the band, top and bottom aligned. Brick/terracotta red. This bar appears on the active item ONLY: I scanned the same 3px column at y 540, 560 and 600 (About Me / My Research Areas) and found plain cream, no red. There is no continuous left rail.
  (c) The label text darkens: "Home" measures 5th-percentile ink 86 versus 106 for the adjacent "About Me" in identical exposure — a real, visible step, possibly a weight bump as well.

HOVER / FOCUS: not captured. The mouse cursor is parked in the content column, not over any nav item, so no hover fill, no focus ring and no transition can be read from this frame.

SIDEBAR BEHAVIOUR: the preview viewport is shorter than the page. A classic scrollbar with ▲ and ▼ arrows sits at x 437-445, track y 212-855, thumb y 312-794 — thumb ≈75% of track, offset downward. The top of the profile photo is clipped flush against the viewport top edge while the content column is mid-scroll, which is consistent with a persistently visible (fixed or sticky, full-viewport-height) sidebar whose own content overflows a short viewport. This matches the professor's one explicit instruction, "sol kisimda menu olcak hep" — there will ALWAYS be a menu on the left. No hamburger, no collapse control, no mobile state is visible; the frame shows a desktop viewport only.
components: Circular avatar / profile portrait — perfect circle, border-radius 50%, 140 photo px diameter (≈36.6% of sidebar width). NO ring, NO border, NO stroke, NO drop shadow, NO background plate. The photo bleeds straight to the circle edge. Top edge clipped by the viewport in this frame.
Name block — serif, medium/semibold, near-black-navy, single line "Korkut Kaynardag, PhD", left-aligned on the common gutter. No underline, no rule beneath it.

Title/affiliation block — three rendered lines of regular-weight sans in mid grey at ≈0.75× the nav size, ≈1.6 line-height, left-aligned. Semantically two fields: the role+department (wrapping after "Civil") and the institution.

Nav link row — a full-bleed 43px-tall interactive band spanning the whole sidebar width, square corners, containing a single left-aligned regular-weight sans label. No icon, no bullet, no chevron, no trailing count, no underline. Inactive state is transparent over the cream.

Active nav link row — the same band filled ≈6% darker in the same hue, plus a flush-left ≈3px brick-red vertical accent bar of identical height, plus a darker label. Square corners, no inset, no rounding, no shadow.

Nav sub-label — a second line beneath a nav label at ≈0.62× size in a lighter grey, NOT indented (shares the parent's left edge), items joined by a spaced middot " · ". Used on exactly one item in this frame.
Content H1 — large serif in a distinctly blue navy, clearly bluer than the sidebar name colour.
Content body paragraph — regular sans, dark grey, generous line-height, with inline BOLD runs used for emphasis ("mysel[f]") and em dashes in running prose.
Horizontal hairline rule — a single-pixel, very low-contrast full-width line used in the content column as a section separator; two instances visible (y≈266 and y≈710).

NOT PRESENT anywhere in the sidebar: buttons, pills, cards, badges, tags, chips, tables, callouts, a search box, a table of contents, social icons, a CTA, a footer block, or any elevation/shadow of any kind.
design.texture_and_effects:
The sidebar is a FLAT warm cream fill with no visible texture, noise, paper grain or linen. The fine vertical striping and moire across every light area is the phone camera beating against the monitor's subpixel grid — a capture artefact, NOT a design texture. Do not reproduce it.

On a possible sidebar gradient: the raw frame does look warmer/yellower at the top and paler/cooler toward the bottom (B/R ratio 0.84 at y210 → 0.76 at y490 → 0.94 at y850). I tested this against the content column at the identical heights and found the SAME trend there (0.94 → 0.90 → 1.06). Since a flat white content area cannot itself be gradient-filled, the top-warm-to-bottom-cool shift is a capture artefact — monitor viewing-angle gamma shift plus glare — not a CSS gradient. Build the sidebar as a FLAT fill, or at most an extremely subtle vertical wash. What IS real is the constant warm offset between sidebar and content, which holds at every single height sampled.

No shadows anywhere: no elevation on the sidebar, no shadow under the avatar, no shadow or border on the active band, no border between the two columns. The only strokes in the entire page are the content column's hairline rules.

No motion can be assessed — this is a single still, not a clip. The rounded corners visible at the top-left and bottom-left of the cream area belong to the claude.ai artifact PREVIEW IFRAME, not to the site design; do not build a rounded card around the sidebar.

notable: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT COLOUR FACT: the sidebar is warm cream/parchment and the content area is cool near-white, and they are separated by NOTHING — no border, no divider, no shadow. I confirmed the warmth offset is real, not camera warmth, by comparing sidebar and content in the same horizontal band at 17 heights: the ratio held at 1.24 R / 1.22 G / 1.10 B at every single one. That stable, two-tone contrast IS the "renkler dizayn" he said he liked. Build the sidebar cream and the content neutral white, and never put a line between them.

THE ACTIVE INDICATOR IS A THREE-PART COMPOUND, not a single highlight: (1) a full-bleed SQUARE-CORNERED band the full width of the sidebar, 43px tall, filled ~6% darker in the same hue — emphatically NOT a rounded pill and NOT inset from the gutter; (2) a ~3px BRICK-RED vertical bar flush against the sidebar's left edge, exactly the same height as the band and top/bottom aligned with it; (3) a darkened label. All three fire together on "Home".

The brick-red accent almost certainly comes from the red brick wall behind him in the profile photo. If you need a second accent or a hover tint, sample from that portrait rather than inventing one — it is the only warm red in the whole composition and it ties the avatar to the nav.

The accent bar is on the ACTIVE ITEM ONLY. I scanned the same 3px column at three inactive rows and found plain cream. Do not build a continuous left rail with a sliding indicator — build a per-item bar.

TWO TYPEFACES, STRICTLY SPLIT BY ROLE: serif for names and headings (his name in the sidebar, the H1 in the content), sans for everything else (subtitle, all nav, all body). Nothing in the sidebar is uppercase, letter-spaced or small-caps. Keeping that split is what makes the draft read academic rather than corporate.
Content H1 navy (~#1B3A5C) is visibly BLUER than the sidebar name ink (~#1A2432). They are two different colours, not one. Worth preserving.

ONE LEFT GUTTER GOVERNS THE WHOLE SIDEBAR at ~5% of its width — photo, name, subtitle, every nav label and the sub-label all start on it. The sub-label is NOT indented under its parent. This flatness is the layout's discipline; indenting the sub-label would break it.

NAV RHYTHM IS A DEAD-CONSTANT 47px PITCH (43px band + 4px gap), and the one row with a sub-label GROWS to 68px rather than compressing its band. Reproduce that: sub-labels push the row taller, they do not squeeze into it.

The photo's top being flush against the viewport edge while the content column is mid-scroll indicates a persistently-visible full-height sidebar whose own content overflows a short viewport — exactly the "sol kisimda menu olcak hep" behaviour. Build it fixed/sticky at 100vh with its own overflow-y, and give it enough top padding that the portrait never clips the way it does here.

The draft is a claude.ai artifact named "Korkut's Research Hub" previewed in a narrow side panel — so everything in this frame was rendered in an unusually NARROW and SHORT viewport. The real site will have far more horizontal room for the content column than this photo suggests; do not size the content measure from what is visible here.

Everything in the sidebar is FLAT. Zero shadows, zero borders, zero elevation, zero rounded cards, no texture. The rounded corners you can see on the cream area belong to the preview iframe, not to the design — do not wrap the sidebar in a rounded card.

The visible content fragments ("…hings: mysel[f]…", "…rtment of Civ[il]…", "…l health monit[oring]…", "…s — deployed…") confirm the body copy is already written prose about structural health monitoring and signal processing — consistent with his "Ben tum icerigi ve figurleri claude den hazirladim zaten". Treat the content as supplied; the job is the shell.
Only ONE inline bold run appears in the visible body copy. Emphasis is used sparingly — keep it that way.
